events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to Grand Haven by boat.** I'd expect it to be about a 1 of 4 (below average) this week. Muskegon is also about a 1, South Haven about a 1, and St. Joseph about a 0. Expect slow fishing everywhere.
- **Troll around the pierheads in 90 to 180 feet of water,** with lines run 45 to 100 feet down. Glow plugs, glow spoons, and meat rigs are the lures to start with.
- **If Grand Haven is slow, try Muskegon** in 70 to 150 feet, 40 to 100 feet down, with the same glow plugs and spoons.
- **Skip St. Joseph for salmon this week.** Its boats found few fish.

## Why

- **Grand Haven is my pick because it is the only port whose latest boat report named a clear fish zone:** the Aug 23 Grand Haven report put the best action at 45 to 100 feet down in 90 to 180 feet of water, even though it rated the fishing slow.
- **I'd expect this week to stay slow because all four ports rated boats 0 in the Aug 23 reports,** and the Aug 23 Grand Haven report called the salmon action slow.
- **Muskegon and Grand Haven had good weeks two weeks ago,** so I'd expect them to recover before St. Joseph and South Haven, where the fish were scattered.
- **I'd expect the lake to stay warm and stable,** since the buoy near Grand Haven and Muskegon was flat at about 67 F over the last week and showed no sharp drop that would bring fish in.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (latest is Aug 23, six days old):**
- Grand Haven (Aug 23): "Boats trolling around the pierheads found the salmon action to be slow… The best action… 45 to 100 down in 90 to 180 feet of water… Glow plugs, glow spoons and meat rigs all worked well." Quality 0.
- Muskegon (Aug 23): "The salmon action has slowed down… a few salmon 40 to 100 feet down in 70 to 150 feet of water." Quality 0.
- South Haven (Aug 23): "Salmon anglers found fishing tough… The fish were very scattered," best at about 100 feet. Quality 0.
- St. Joseph (Aug 23): "Salmon anglers had a hard time locating fish." Quality 0.
- Two weeks earlier (Aug 16), Grand Haven, Muskegon, and South Haven boats all rated 3 (good). Grand Haven's Aug 16 report followed an upwelling-type drop of 8 F in buoy temperature.

**Past seasons (history, not current conditions):**
- Similar water temperatures in late August in past years (2022, 2023) gave mostly average to slow boat fishing, with fish often scattered and found at 100 to 200 feet of water (Grand Haven, 2022-08-24; Muskegon, 2022-08-24).

**Conditions now:**
- The conditions tool was in backtest mode, so these are the week-before summaries, not live data. Buoy surface water averaged 67 F near Grand Haven and Muskegon (flat over the week), 70 F at South Haven (down 1 F), and 72 F at St. Joseph (down 1 F).
- No wind forecast was returned, so I can't judge wind for this trip.

## Caveats

- The newest report is from Aug 23, about six days old, and the conditions data is a week-before summary rather than live data. Check the latest DNR bulletin and the current forecast before you go.
- Ratings are my estimates from slow reports. They are not a prediction of catches.
- Past seasons are general history and may not repeat this year.

- Aug 9, 2023 DNR bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/369e344
